title_en: What Wall Street Really Thinks About the AI Trade Now
title_zh: 华尔街现在究竟怎么看 AI 交易
subtitle_zh: 巴克莱全球股票战术策略主管 Alexander Altmann 做客 Odd Lots：neocloud 的融资裂缝、AI 泡沫的“否认”阶段、资本竞争与净发行，以及为什么个股剧烈波动、VIX 却依然平静。
description: What Wall Street Really Thinks About the AI Trade Now

turns.en: Bloomberg Audio Studios. Podcasts.
turns.zh: 彭博音频工作室（Bloomberg Audio Studios）。播客。

turns.en: Radio. News.
turns.zh: 广播。新闻。

turns.en: Hello and welcome to another episode of the All Thoughts Podcast. I'm Traci Allaway.
turns.zh: 大家好，欢迎收听新一期的 Odd Lots 播客。我是崔西·阿洛韦（Tracy Alloway）。

turns.en: And I'm Joe Weisenthal.
turns.zh: 我是乔·韦森塔尔（Joe Weisenthal）。

turns.en: Joe, interesting times in markets.
turns.zh: 乔，眼下市场可真是有意思。

turns.en: You know what?
turns.zh: 你知道吗？

turns.en: What?
turns.zh: 怎么了？

turns.en: I kind of feel like I lost the plot.
turns.zh: 我有点感觉自己已经跟不上剧情了。

turns.en: I know.
turns.zh: 我也是。

turns.en: I was like, I had this realization. I don't know what anything's going on anymore. We're just talking markets. And obviously I lost the plot with life in general. Like no one's disputed that. But just as like, what are the consensus trades these days? Like what are people actually worried about with some of these data center stuff? Like what, Corweave, what, et cetera. I have no idea what anyone thinks anymore. Like I need a reality check badly.
turns.zh: 我这么说吧，我突然意识到，我已经完全搞不清现在到底在发生什么了。我们就在那儿聊市场。当然，我对整个人生都已经失去了方向感——这一点没人否认。但单说市场，现在所谓的共识交易到底是什么？对于这些数据中心的东西，人们究竟在担心什么？什么 CoreWeave 之类的。我真的不知道现在任何人是怎么想的了。我特别需要一次现实校准（reality check）。

turns.en: So we're recording this on October 28th. And in terms of market reality checks, we're actually doing better on this one because we often end up recording these right before a Fed decision or right before an S-1 comes out or right before earnings guidance or something. This time, we've timed it pretty well. So we just had the FOMC decision. Earlier this week, we had the S-1 filing from Anthropic. During the Fed presser, Oracle came out with some additional guidance. There's a lot of stuff going on, even though we're going to be able to talk about some of it. There's more stuff coming up later this week. And so I feel like it's a really good moment in time to kind of stop and figure out what's going on.
turns.zh: 我们这期节目是在10月28日录制的。要说市场的现实校准，这一次我们的时机其实相当不错，因为我们经常是在美联储决议之前、或者某份 S-1 招股书公布之前、或者财报指引出来之前赶着录。这次我们卡得挺准。所以，本周早些时候 FOMC（联邦公开市场委员会）决议刚刚出炉，Anthropic 的 S-1 文件也提交了，美联储发布会期间甲骨文（Oracle）又额外给出了一些指引。事情非常多，尽管我们只能聊其中一部分。本周晚些时候还会有更多。所以我觉得，这正是一个停下来好好梳理一下当前局势的绝佳时点。

turns.en: What's going on? So you mentioned Oracle had some investor day data coming out. The stock is up 12%. I know. I would say this was a bigger story today than the FOMC.
turns.zh: 到底在发生什么？你提到甲骨文公布了一些投资者日的数据。股价涨了12%。我知道。我会说，今天这件事比 FOMC 更重要。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: Right. Like the questions about Capital expenditures, how much debt the big hyperscalers and so forth are going to take on. Clearly, I would say in the minds of many participants, much bigger questions than like, oh, did they are going to hold in October or whatever.
turns.zh: 对吧。比如关于资本开支的问题，那些大型超大规模云厂商（hyperscaler）要背负多少债务等等。显然，我会说，在很多市场参与者的心目中，这些问题远比“哦，他们10月会不会按兵不动”要大得多。

turns.en: Not a high bar given Kevin Warsh's ability to deflect.
turns.zh: 考虑到凯文·沃什（Kevin Warsh）打太极的本事，这个门槛可不高。

turns.en: I tuned in for a few minutes of that press conference.
turns.zh: 那场新闻发布会我收看了几分钟。

turns.en: But you're right.
turns.zh: 不过你说得对。

turns.en: That guy's good at not saying that.
turns.zh: 那人真的很擅长什么都不说。

turns.en: All right. Well, we do in fact have the perfect guest. We're going to be speaking with someone who we've had on the podcast before. Last time we were talking about levered ETFs. This time we're going to get a general sort of market overview. It's Alex Altman, Global Head of Equities Tactical Strategies over at Barclays. So Alex, thank you so much for coming back on OddLots.
turns.zh: 好吧。事实上，我们请到了最合适的嘉宾。我们要对话的这位，之前来过我们节目。上一次我们聊的是杠杆 ETF。这一次我们要做一个更宏观的市场综述。他就是巴克莱（Barclays）全球股票战术策略主管亚历克斯·阿尔特曼（Alex Altmann）。Alex，非常感谢你再次做客 Odd Lots。

turns.en: Thank you very much for having me again.
turns.zh: 非常感谢再次邀请我。

turns.en: So what's going on? No, I mean, is there like a consensus AI outlook at the moment?
turns.zh: 那么现在到底怎么回事？我是说，目前市场对 AI 有没有一个共识性的展望？

turns.en: Yeah, there is.
turns.zh: 有的。

turns.en: The consensus AI outlook is that AI is still going to, this train is in motion. We're not stopping this train. That's still the consensus, to be very clear. And let's say if you were to sort of take a sample of a bunch of investors across different cohorts, whether it's in the US, Europe, Asia, and ask them, gun to their head, do you want to still be bullish or bearish the AI story? You're going to get an overwhelming positive answer.
turns.zh: 对 AI 的共识展望是：AI 还会继续下去，这列火车已经在动，我们停不下它。这仍然是共识，我要把这点说得非常清楚。而且，假设你去抽样一大批不同类别的投资者——不管是美国的、欧洲的还是亚洲的——拿枪指着他们问：你现在还想看多还是看空 AI 这个故事？你会得到一个压倒性的正面回答。

turns.en: Yeah. Right.
turns.zh: 嗯，对。

turns.en: And we can debate like where people are on the position scale, but like that's the general view. Right. And this is why I think that if you, you know, you've probably seen that chart of where we are in like the bubble kind of thing. And then as it begins to roll over, the first dip down is the denial one.
turns.zh: 我们可以争论大家在仓位刻度上处于什么位置，但这就是大体的看法。对吧。这也是为什么——你大概见过那张图，画的是我们在泡沫曲线上的位置，然后当它开始掉头向下时，第一个下探的阶段就是“否认”。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: I'm not going to say we're at kind of this bubbles popped. I know there's commentary out there that actually has said that, but I definitely, if you were to sort of juxtapose those two narratives, we're in the denial phase right now because everyone is still extremely bullish.
turns.zh: 我不会说我们已经走到了“泡沫破裂”那一步。我知道外面确实有些评论这么说，但如果你把这两种叙事并排放在一起看，我们现在处于“否认”阶段，因为每个人都还极度看多。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: You got guys saying like, oh, semiconductors, you got Hynix or whatever, or some of these Korean memory stocks, they're on three times earnings. I'm like, you can look up three times earnings on a Bloomberg terminal. That requires no work at all.
turns.zh: 有人在说，哦，半导体，你看海力士（SK Hynix）之类的，或者一些韩国内存股，它们的市盈率只有三倍。我就想说，你在彭博终端上一查就能看到三倍市盈率，这根本不需要花什么功夫。

turns.en: Right.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: So everyone is out there.
turns.zh: 所以市场上大家都在这么找标的。

turns.en: Thank you for plugging the utility of the Bloomberg terminal, by the way.
turns.zh: 顺便说一句，谢谢你为彭博终端的实用性打广告。

turns.en: What do you mean there are 3X earnings?
turns.zh: 你说“三倍市盈率”是什么意思？

turns.en: There are memory stocks that are.
turns.zh: 确实有些内存股就是这个估值。

turns.en: They're traded with an EPS, not an EPS, a PE of three. Correct. Because people there is. And because the perception is that we're at such a peak and we know how cyclical of an industry it is that when the earnings are this good, you're not going to pay up for them. Exactly.
turns.zh: 它们的交易估值是——不是 EPS，是市盈率（P/E）三倍。没错。因为人们的认知是，我们正处在这样一个周期高点，而大家又清楚这个行业的周期性有多强，所以当盈利好到这种程度的时候，你是不会给出高估值的。正是如此。

turns.en: The old mantra is you don't buy cyclical companies, especially ones as historically cyclical as semiconductors, when they're at peak earnings.
turns.zh: 老话是这么说的：不要在周期股盈利见顶的时候买入，尤其是像半导体这样在历史上周期性极强的公司。

turns.en: I didn't realize they were that low. Okay. So let's put some pieces together. So we have the fact that the P.E. is actually quite low. People do not expect exponential growth from the memory companies in terms of their EPS anytime soon as implied by the P.E.
turns.zh: 我没想到它们的估值低到这个程度。好，那我们把几块拼图拼起来。所以，事实是市盈率其实相当低；从市盈率隐含的意思来看，人们并不预期内存公司的 EPS 短期内会指数级增长。

turns.en: Ratios.
turns.zh: 比率。

turns.en: What is going on with the neoclouds? Why is it that despite, as you say, the consensus is bullish, still everyone wants to be long, the AI trade, suddenly there's all this anxiety about, you know, people are quoting Corweave CDS charts.
turns.zh: 那 neocloud（新型云服务商）到底怎么了？为什么就像你说的，共识依然看多，所有人都还想做多 AI 交易，却突然冒出这么多焦虑情绪？大家开始到处转发 CoreWeave 的 CDS（信用违约互换）走势图。

turns.en: Sure.
turns.zh: 好。

turns.en: All right.
turns.zh: 行。

turns.en: So let's take a step back for a second, right? Because I want to talk about neoclouds in the context of the broader AI ecosystem. So obviously neoclouds are a group of businesses that are effectively in some way, shape or form mandated to build compute, which they will then sell to predetermined customers, some of which predetermined, some of them will be speculative. Regardless of what you may believe in that business model or not, these are tip of the spear. These businesses don't have operating cash flow today or minimal operating cash flow today in many cases. And so they represent the riskier part of the financing aspect of the AI spectrum.
turns.zh: 那我们先后退一步，好吗？因为我想把 neocloud 放在整个 AI 生态系统的大背景下来谈。显然，neocloud 是这么一类企业：它们某种程度上被要求去建设算力，然后再把这些算力卖给既定的客户——其中一部分客户是事先约定的，另一部分则是投机性的。不管你是否认同这种商业模式，它们都是“矛尖”（tip of the spear，最前沿、最先承受冲击的位置）。这些公司今天没有经营性现金流，或者在很多情况下经营性现金流微乎其微。所以它们代表了 AI 融资链条中风险更高的那一端。

turns.en: Right.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: And I think that's, that's an irrefutable fact. You know, people can talk about, well, actually they're REITs in disguise and actually they're not, they're nowhere near as risky as people think they are.
turns.zh: 而且我认为，这是一个无可辩驳的事实。人们可以说，哎呀其实它们是变相的 REITs（房地产投资信托），其实它们远没有大家以为的那么危险。

turns.en: Sure.
turns.zh: 好。

turns.en: Let's have that debate. But compared to say the hyperscalers, whether it's, you know, the Googles and the Amazons who have got huge, I mean, they're cash volcano businesses. They are different, different sort of category. And the reason I want to make that distinction is because if you think of neoclouds as periphery and hyperscalers as core.
turns.zh: 这个我们可以辩。但和超大规模云厂商相比——不管是谷歌还是亚马逊，它们体量巨大，我是说，它们是“现金火山”型的生意。它们是完全不同的类别。我之所以要强调这个区分，是因为如果你把 neocloud 看作外围、把超大规模云厂商看作核心，

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: And I want you to draw a parallel, not directly, cause I'm not trying to make some sensationalist statement here, but draw a parallel to the GFC. Right. The problem doesn't didn't start with GC banks.
turns.zh: 我想让你做一个类比——不是直接的类比，因为我并不是要在这里说什么耸人听闻的话——而是和全球金融危机（GFC）做类比。对吧，问题并不是从大型银行开始的。

turns.en: Right.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: It started with subprime vehicles, 12, 18, 24 months beforehand.
turns.zh: 它是从次贷这个载体开始的，比危机爆发早了12、18、24个月。

turns.en: Right.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: And so what's I find most interesting is that there is evidently a financing problem within Neo clouds, right? That is evident Cypher try to, they did their convert. nuked their own share price in doing so because they clearly couldn't tap the debt markets directly.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得最有意思的是，neocloud 内部显然存在一个融资问题。这一点很明显：Cipher 试着去融资，他们发了可转债，结果把自己的股价砸了下去，因为他们显然没法直接进入债券市场融资。

turns.en: I don't even know who. Cypher?
turns.zh: 我都不知道 Cipher 是谁？

turns.en: It's another neocloud. Exactly. A company that you've never heard of. And yet the reason why CoreWeave bonds sold off was not because of CoreWeave. They didn't say anything that week. It was because Cypher, another neocloud, tried to tap financing. And in doing so, materially hurt their own share price. And then all of a sudden, a bunch of investors, quick off the mark, put two and two together.
turns.zh: 它是另一家 neocloud。没错。一家你从来没听说过的公司。但 CoreWeave 的债券之所以遭到抛售，原因并不在 CoreWeave 本身——那一周他们什么也没说。是因为 Cipher，另一家 neocloud，试图融资，而这么做严重伤害了它自己的股价。然后突然之间，一批反应很快的投资者就把这两件事联系到了一起。

turns.en: Right.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: And then it spilled over, but like, quite frankly, if you look at the data center bonds in isolation, whether like the beignets of this.
turns.zh: 接着就外溢了。但坦白说，如果你单独看数据中心债券——不管是 Beignet 这一类的，

turns.en: World, you know, the meta one, exactly.
turns.zh: 这一类的，你知道，就是 Meta 那只，没错。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: These had already been widening. For months prior to that.
turns.zh: 这些债券在那之前的好几个月就已经在走阔了。

turns.en: Right.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: And we'd seen a creep in IG hyperscale is one of.
turns.zh: 我们也看到投资级（IG）超大规模云厂商那一类出现了利差的缓慢爬升，其中一家是

turns.en: These ones that pivoted from Bitcoin mining to getting into AI.
turns.zh: 就是那些从比特币挖矿转型做 AI 的公司。

turns.en: Yeah. Yeah. All right.
turns.zh: 嗯，嗯。好。

turns.en: So I guess the point I'm trying to make is, is that there's ripple effects in financing that start in. in the periphery, and we're seeing that. So what I find amazing, back to the original point in terms of you asked what's going on, are people bullish or bearish, and we literally just conducted a survey with a group of investors.
turns.zh: 所以我想说的重点是，融资领域存在涟漪效应，它从外围开始扩散，而我们正在看到这一幕。回到最初的问题——你问到底在发生什么，大家是看多还是看空——我们刚刚对一组投资者做了一项调查。

turns.en: Fantastic.
turns.zh: 太好了。

turns.en: Yeah. And the only, I mean, you could make this argument, this is a high number, but from the responses that we've got so far, around about 60% of investors, we asked them a question, do you think financing is going to be a problem? AI financing is going to be a problem for the foreseeable future.
turns.zh: 是的。而且唯一——我是说，你可以这么论证，说这个比例算高的——但从我们目前收到的回复来看，大约60%的投资者……我们问他们一个问题：你认为融资会成为一个问题吗？AI 融资在可预见的未来会成为一个问题吗？

turns.en: Only 60% said yes.
turns.zh: 只有60%的人说“是”？

turns.en: By definition, what's happened over the past couple of weeks means the answer should be 100%, right? And yet, let's just call it just over half think or just under half think there is no financing issue, but there is. So what's happening in AI to me is evidence of like almost a denial of a reality that's already here.
turns.zh: 从定义上讲，过去几周发生的事情意味着答案本该是100%，对吧？然而，我们就这么说吧：刚刚过半的人认为是，或者说将近一半的人认为不存在融资问题——但问题是实实在在存在的。所以在我看来，AI 领域正在发生的这一切，几乎就是对一个已经摆在眼前的现实的否认。

turns.en: To be fair, one of the reasons CoreWeave started selling off was because Brandon McBee gave an interview to the FT where he was talking literally about unlimited amounts of borrowing, which I think ties into what you're discussing when it comes to capital concerns. So on the financing side, I mean, we've seen some differentiation in terms of lending money to different AI entities out there. Is the overarching point that we've been in a period where it seemed like there was in fact unlimited money and people could tap the IG markets or the loan markets for as much as they needed. And now we're moving to a period where things are more selective and not everyone is going to be able to get the type of funding that they were tapping before.
turns.zh: 说句公道话，CoreWeave 开始遭到抛售的原因之一，是 Brannin McBee 接受了《金融时报》（FT）的采访，在采访中他实打实地谈到了“无限量”的举债——我觉得这正好呼应了你所说的那种对资本的担忧。所以在融资这一侧，我们已经看到，市场在向市面上不同的 AI 主体放贷时出现了一些分化。那么核心的要点是不是：我们此前处在一个看起来资金无限的阶段，人们想融多少就能从投资级债市或贷款市场融到多少；而现在我们正在转向一个更加挑剔的阶段，不是每个人都能再拿到以前那种规模的资金了。

turns.en: That is exactly it.
turns.zh: 完全正确。

turns.en: Right. Because, you know, part of the job that my team does is we travel the world. We talk to a lot of different investors and, We ask questions, we collate the kind of feedback that informs our decisions. And there was this almost universal view that, and you guys would have heard it as well, AI was immune to high interest rates. Evidently is not true, right? And so there is a spectrum. And even, I think that's where I think the meta results were pretty instructive in the 14C, in the sense that they highlighted the fact that financing does constrain, financing does have limitations. And we wrote a load of, we did a load of work on this in the summer where we were looking, not specifically at AI, we were just looking at the holistic net issuance profile of the market. And maybe you guys saw this. And we looked at just the entire corporate market, so IG high yield. We looked at treasuries and we looked at, equity. And we went back to about 1995, collated all the data, and looked at each market, the amount of net issuance in any given year as a percentage of each market's market cap in that given year. And then we plotted it over time. And what we found was there was, unsurprisingly, a very strong relationship. When interest rates went down, overall issuance went up, and vice versa, as you'd expect.
turns.zh: 对。因为你知道，我团队工作的一部分就是跑遍全球，和大量不同的投资者交流，我们提问、我们汇总各种反馈，用来指导我们的判断。当时几乎是一种普遍的看法——你们肯定也听到过——就是 AI 对高利率免疫。显然这不是真的，对吧？所以这里面是有一个谱系的。而且我觉得，Meta 那次财报在这方面（14C）颇具启发意义，它凸显了一个事实：融资是有约束的，融资是有局限的。今年夏天我们就此做了大量研究，我们看的并不是专门针对 AI，而是看整个市场的净发行全景。也许你们也看到了。我们考察了整个公司债市场，也就是投资级和高收益级；我们看了国债，也看了股票。我们把数据回溯到大约1995年，把所有数据汇总起来，针对每个市场计算任意一年的净发行额占该市场当年市值的百分比。然后我们把它按时间画出来。我们发现——毫不意外——两者之间存在非常强的关系：利率下行时，整体发行量上升；反之亦然，正如你所预期的那样。

turns.en: The laws of the economy still exist.
turns.zh: 经济规律还是存在的嘛。

turns.en: Well, apparently not so much in 2025 and 2026.
turns.zh: 嗯，看起来在2025年和2026年就不太存在了。

turns.en: Yeah, here's the punchline.
turns.zh: 是啊，这就是关键所在。

I can leverage that too, through the prime prime businesses. The problem is, is that you've effectively tripled more than tripled the AUM plus obviously leverage.
